column1: # comment: Deception / falsehood / misinformation alignments (#213). FORMAL GROUNDING: gmeow:heldStandpoint / gmeow:projectedStandpoint realise the divergence model of deception as standpoint-indexed claims; gmeow:bullshit is the Frankfurt modality integrated into the Standpoint-Logic value space. schema.org: ClaimReview is an attestation act (not a truth verdict); Rating is a lossy projection to VerificationResult. CRMinf: I6_Belief_Value aligns to gmeow:StandpointModality (including the bullshit modality); I1_Argumentation is referenced for the solver-layer argument-acceptability function. PROV-O: deception events are prov:Activity; standpoint claims are prov:Entity. Wikidata: wd:Q170028 (deception) aligns to gmeow:eventTypeDeception. AIF (Argument Interchange Format) is referenced in the solver layer (fnArgumentAcceptability) but not aligned via TermEquivalence because AIF lacks a stable, resolvable RDF namespace suitable for SSSOM rows.

column6: a deception event is a provenance activity; the specific deception semantics are GMEOW-specific and not entailed by PROV-O
a standpoint claim (held or projected) is a provenance entity attributed to its standpoint agent
GMEOW's StandpointModality (unequivocal/probable/conceivable/refuted/bullshit) spans and extends CRMinf's I6 Belief Value
an attribution of deceptive intent is an argumentation act in the CRMinf sense; acceptability is computed externally (Principle 12)
Wikidata 'deception' (Q170028) — the act of propagating beliefs that are not true

schema:ClaimReview is a fact-checking act; in GMEOW it is an Attestation with attestationTypeFactCheck. The single-verdict model of ClaimReview is a lossy projection — GMEOW keeps every standpoint's assessment as a coexisting claim.
schema:Rating (the outcome of a ClaimReview) projects to gmeow:VerificationResult — a lossy downcast dropping the standpoint axis and confidence.
